title: The Machine Learning Paradigm
description: Discover how machine learning differs from traditional programming. Compare Supervised, Unsupervised, and Reinforcement Learning.

slides.title: Software 1.0 vs Software 2.0 💻
slides.content:
# The Machine Learning Paradigm

In classical software engineering (**Software 1.0**), human programmers write explicit logical rules that process data to produce answers.

In Machine Learning (**Software 2.0**), we feed both historical data and desired answers into a learning algorithm, which *synthesizes the underlying rules automatically*.

$$\text{Traditional: } \text{Data} + \text{Rules} \longrightarrow \text{Answers}$$
$$\text{Machine Learning: } \text{Data} + \text{Answers} \longrightarrow \text{Rules (Model)}$$

slides.title: The Three Pillars of Machine Learning 🏛️
slides.content:
# The Three Learning Paradigms

Machine learning is partitioned into three foundational branches:

| Learning Paradigm | Training Data Format | Supervision Signal | Objective | Standard Algorithms |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Supervised Learning** | Features $\mathbf{X}$ paired with Labels $\mathbf{y}$ | Direct target ground truth | Learn predictive mapping $\hat{y} = f(\mathbf{x})$ | Linear Regression, Random Forest, SVM, XGBoost |
| **Unsupervised Learning** | Features $\mathbf{X}$ only (no labels) | None (self-guided) | Uncover hidden geometry, clusters, distributions | K-Means, PCA, DBSCAN, t-SNE |
| **Reinforcement Learning** | States $s$, Actions $a$, Rewards $r$ | Scalar environmental reward | Discover policy $\pi(s)$ maximizing cumulative reward | Q-Learning, PPO, Deep Q-Networks (DQN) |

* **Supervised:** Teacher grades every exam question.
* **Unsupervised:** Student organizes a library without titles.
* **Reinforcement:** Puppy learns tricks through treats and scolds.

quizData.question: Grouping online retail shoppers into distinct personas based solely on their browsing histories without pre-assigned customer category labels is an example of which paradigm?
quizData.explanation: Because there are no target category labels provided and the goal is to discover latent clusters in the feature space, it is Unsupervised Learning.

slides.title: AI Pro Tip: The Data-Centric AI Mindset 💡
slides.content:
## Andrew Ng's Data-Centric Philosophy
Historically, AI researchers spent 80% of their effort iterating on model architectures while holding the training dataset fixed.

Modern production engineering has flipped this: holding the model constant and systematically cleaning, labeling, and augmenting training data delivers substantially higher gains in accuracy and reliability than hyperparameter tuning alone!
